Topics · Prayer and closeness to God

Asked about God, why is the answer so direct?

Answers in the Quran come through the word Say. Asked about God Himself, it is gone. Here is what that shows.

Part 1 of 4

﴿يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْأَهِلَّةِ ۖ قُلْ هِىَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلْحَجِّ ۗ وَلَيْسَ ٱلْبِرُّ بِأَن تَأْتُوا۟ ٱلْبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلْبِرَّ مَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ ۗ وَأْتُوا۟ ٱلْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَٰبِهَا ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

They ask you, [O Muḥammad], about the crescent moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for ḥajj [pilgrimage]." And it is not righteousness to enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allāh. And enter houses from their doors. And fear Allāh that you may succeed.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:189

Translation

God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years;

Original · Hebrew

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יְהִ֤י מְאֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַיּ֖וֹם וּבֵ֣ין הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָי֤וּ לְאֹתֹת֙ וּלְמ֣וֹעֲדִ֔ים וּלְיָמִ֖ים וְשָׁנִֽים׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 1:14

World English Bible

﴿وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ ۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they ask you, [O Muḥammad], about the soul. Say, "The soul is of the affair [i.e., concern] of my Lord. And you [i.e., mankind] have not been given of knowledge except a little."

Quran · Al-Isra 17:85

Translation

But there is a spirit in man, and the Spirit of the Almighty gives them understanding.

Original · Hebrew

אָ֭כֵן רֽוּחַ־הִ֣יא בֶאֱנ֑וֹשׁ וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּבִינֵֽם׃

Job · 32:8

World English Bible

The Quran keeps people's questions, and it keeps to a form. They ask you about the new moons, about wine, about the spoils of war, about the soul. Then comes one word: Say. The phrase “they ask you” appears fifteen times. In fourteen the reply passes through that word, and the fifteenth, about the hour of the end, gets no date at all. The form has a plain meaning. The Prophet stands between the question and the reply, and carries it.

A question for you

In those verses, what does the word Say do?

If you sayIt tells the Prophet to carry the answer.
ThenThen the word marks a role: someone stands between the question and the reply. Keep that role in view, because it is about to change.
If you sayIt is only a habit of style.
ThenThen its absence should mean little. That is a fair test, and the next verse lets you run it.
If you sayI would need to read more of them.
ThenThe list is short and checkable: fifteen places. Reading them is the whole of the method here.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:186

Translation

Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 145:18

World English Bible

Then one verse opens differently. This time the question is about God Himself, the largest a person can ask, and the expected word does not come. The reply starts at once, in the first person: I am near. If those answers place a carrier between question and reply, leaving him out here does something. The verse says God is near, and its wording shows it, in the space where a word was expected.

A question for you

What changes when the word is taken out?

If you sayThe answer reaches the asker directly.
ThenThat is how the wording reads against the pattern. What you do with it is the next question, and it belongs to you.
If you sayNothing. It is a matter of style.
ThenThen nearness rests on the plain statement alone, and the statement stands: I am near. The missing word is a sign, and the sentence holds without it.
If you sayI feel something I cannot explain yet.
ThenThe verse does not ask for an explanation first. It says who is near and what He does when called.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ٱدْعُونِىٓ أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِى سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.

Quran · Ghafir 40:60

Translation

‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great and difficult things, which you don’t know.’

Original · Hebrew

קְרָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וְאֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ וְאַגִּ֧ידָה לְּךָ֛ גְּדֹל֥וֹת וּבְצֻר֖וֹת לֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽם׃

Jeremiah · 33:3

World English Bible

A sentence about nearness could be mere description. So the Quran also puts it as an invitation with a promise attached: call on Me, and I will answer. Nearness, permission and a promise now stand together. The verse sets no condition of rank, birth, language or place. It closes with a grave word for those too proud to turn to Him, so pride is the one barrier it names. Distance is not on the list.

A question for you

What does the verse ask of the caller before it promises an answer?

If you sayOnly that they call.
ThenThen the first step is small enough for anyone. Elsewhere the Quran asks for sincerity and a response in return, which is what any honest conversation asks.
If you sayA certain rank or standing.
ThenLook for it in the verse. If rank were required, it would appear in these few words. Other verses ask for sincerity, and rank does not come up.
If you sayI am not sure I would qualify.
ThenMany people feel this, and the feeling has a verse that speaks to it. It is worth reading now.

Part 4 of 4

﴿قَالُوا۟ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا ٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا خَـٰطِـِٔينَ٩٧ قَالَ سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّىٓ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ٩٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

They said, "O our father, ask for us forgiveness of our sins; indeed, we have been sinners." He said, "I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Quran · Yusuf 12:97-98

Here is what the missing word does not say. It does not say that others may not pray for you. Jacob's sons ask their father to seek forgiveness for them, and he says he will ask his Lord. That is family love, and the Quran keeps it. A person can ask the living to pray. Their own call needs no one to carry it. And the Prophet loses nothing here. He recited this verse to us, and by reciting it he brought people to God, which was his whole work.

A question for you

Which of these is closest to how you now see it?

If you saySomeone may pray for me, and my own call needs no one.
ThenThen you hold both things the verses hold. There is more on asking the living to pray, if you want it.
If you sayI still feel I need someone, or God will not hear me.
ThenMany people feel this, often out of humility. That feeling deserves its own answer, and it has one.
If you sayI would rather ask no one but God.
ThenThat is open to you. The verses leave room for it, and they also leave room for the friend who prays for you unasked.
